Daily Transit Intelligence
June 20, 2026 — 12 papers analyzed
KEY FINDINGS
Free public transit fare policy may do more for social justice in autonomous
mobility-on-demand systems than regulating or capping the AMoD service itself.
Average on-time performance, the metric agencies obsess over, is a weak
predictor of rider satisfaction; a single bad moment plus a bad ending
dominates the memory of an entire trip.
Congestion pricing's transit ridership gains spread well beyond the tolled
zone, while its travel-demand reduction stays geographically concentrated,
meaning the costs and benefits of the policy land on different neighborhoods.
PAPER OF THE DAY
Risk-Aware Planning for Transit Desert Remediation Under Demand Uncertainty
Polina Khoroshevskaya, Ashish Kumar Perukari
Framing transit-desert remediation as a partially observable Markov decision process with
financial risk constraints, this study shows a belief-aware planner remediates more transit
deserts at lower financial risk than static optimization across 25 US cities.
Why it matters: It tackles transit's foundational chicken-and-egg problem (no service means no
ridership data means no justification for service) with a rigorous, deployable POMDP framework,

ACTIONABLE TAKEAWAYS
Agencies piloting congestion pricing should plan for transit capacity increases beyond the
cordon boundary, not just within it, since ridership gains diffuse outward.
Customer experience teams should target the single worst moment and trip endings in service
design reviews rather than chasing uniform average improvements.
Cities planning AMoD/robotaxi regulation should model free or subsidized transit fares as an
equity lever before reaching for AMoD price caps or budget limits, which this research shows
Transit agencies investing in AI/ML forecasting tools should first invest in the underlying
data-architecture problem (fragmented AFC/APC/AVL/GTFS pipelines), since model quality is
Service planners addressing transit deserts can adopt risk-aware, belief-updating sequential
planning instead of waiting for ridership data that will never exist without service.
